name: Question 16
problem:
Consider a function $y(t)$ such that its Laplace transform is $L{y(t)}=Y(s)$ for $s>{s}_{0}.$ Suppose we wish to find $L{{e}^{4t}y(t)}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write 

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{4t}y(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-2}}\,y(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 16
?
Consider a function y(t) such that its Laplace transform is L{y(t)}=Y(s) for s>s0. Suppose we wish to find L{e4ty(t)}. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write

 
e−st⋅e−4ty(t)
est⋅e4ty(t)
est⋅e−4ty(t)
e−st⋅e4ty(t)
 
e(s+4)t
e−(s+4)t
e−(s−4)t
e(s−4)t
 
Y(s−4)
Y(s)
Y(s+4)
 
s>s0+4
s>s0−4
s>s0
L{e4ty(t)}=∫0∞{(e−st⋅e−4ty(t))(S0)}dt=∫0∞{(e(s+4)t)(S1)}y(t)dt={(Y(s−4))(S2)}for{(s>s0+4)(S3)}.
